items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.summary: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. items.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
items.summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. How Deep Agents Manages Context: Offloading and Summarization
items.summary: The longer an agent runs, the more instructions and tool results pile into its context window, and the worse its reasoning tends to get. That's context rot. This video walks through two context engineering techniques the Deep Agents harness ships out of the box: offloading, which keeps large tool results and long messages out of context while saving them to a virtual file system, and summarization, which compacts the conversation once token usage crosses a threshold (85% by default).
